dyad: A set of two elements treated as one; a pair.
dyadic: Pertaining to a dyad, the number two; of two parts or elements.
dyadically: In a dyadic manner; as a dyad or by means of dyads.
dybbuk: A malicious possessing spirit, believed to be the dislocated soul of a dead person.
dye: A colorant, especially one that has an affinity to the substrate to which it is applied.
dyeability: Quality or degree of being dyeable.

dyeing: present participle and gerund of dye
dyer: One who dyes, especially one who dyes cloth etc.
dyestuff: Any soluble pigment used for dyeing the hair, fabric, etc.
dyewood: Any wood (including bark) from which colouring matter is extracted for dyeing.
dying: Approaching death; about to die; moribund.
dyke: An earthwork raised to prevent inundation of low land by the sea or flooding rivers.
dynamically: In a dynamic way: variably, changingly.
dynamics: The branch of mechanics that is concerned with the effects of forces on the motion of objects.
dynamism: Great energy, drive, force, or power; vigour of body, mind, or personality; oomph or pizzazz.
dynamist: A subscriber to the philosophy of dynamism.
dynamite: A class of explosives made from nitroglycerine in an absorbent medium such as kieselguhr, used in mining and blasting.
dynamited: simple past and past participle of dynamite
dynamiter: A person who uses dynamite, especially one who uses it unlawfully.
dynamites: third-person singular simple present indicative of dynamite
dynamiting: present participle and gerund of dynamite
dynamo: An electricity generator; a dynamo-electric machine.
dynamometer: Any of various devices used to measure mechanical power, force, or torque.
dynamometry: The measurement of forces doing work.
dynamotor: A device for converting electrical power to another form.
dynast: A ruler or governor, especially a hereditary ruler or someone who founded or is part of a dynasty.
dynasty: A series of rulers or dynasts from one family.

dyne: A unit of force in the CGS system; the force required to accelerate a mass of one gram by one centimetre per second per second.
dynein: Any of a group of enzymes that hydrolyze ATP and thus provide motive power for motile structures such as microtubules.
dynel: A type of synthetic fiber used in fibre-reinforced plastic composite materials, especially for marine applications.
dynode: Any of a series of electrodes within a photomultiplier tube.

dyscrasia: Imbalance of the four bodily humors (blood, black and yellow bile, phlegm) that was thought to cause disease.
dysenteric: Of, relating, or pertaining to dysentery

dysfunction: A failure to function in an expected or complete manner.
dysfunctional: Not performing its proper or intended function.
dysgenic: Of or relating to, or causing degeneration or deterioration in offspring.
dyskinesia: A state of involuntary muscle movements, like tics and torticollis, and reduced voluntary muscle movements.
dyslexia: A learning disability characterized by reading and writing difficulties.
dysmenorrhea: Painful menstruation (menstrual pain), viewed as a symptom in any of various disorders.
dysmenorrheic: Of, pertaining to, or experiencing dysmenorrhea.
dyspepsia: Any mild disorder of digestion characterised by stomach pain, discomfort, heartburn, and nausea, often following a meal.
dyspeptic: Of, relating to, or having dyspepsia or indigestion.
dysphasia: Loss of or deficiency in the power to use or understand language as a result of injury or disease of the brain.
dysphemism: The use of a word or phrase carrying negative connotations or imagery (especially one that is derogatory, offensive or vulgar) to replace a (more) neutral original.
dysphemistic: Of, pertaining to, or being a dysphemism.
dysphonia: A difficulty in producing vocal sounds.
dysphoria: A state of feeling unwell or unhappy; a feeling of emotional and mental discomfort and suffering from restlessness, malaise, depression, or anxiety.
dysphoric: Pertaining to dysphoria, or of being in a state of dysphoria.
dysplasia: Abnormal development of cells or tissue, often a precancerous stage of growth.
dyspneal: Pertaining to, or of the nature of dyspnea; in connexion with dyspnea.
dyspneic: Afflicted with dyspnea; possessing unhealthy breathing.
dysprosium: A metallic chemical element (symbol Dy) with atomic number 66: a rare earth element with a metallic silver lustre.
dysrhythmia: A disturbance to an otherwise normal biological rhythm, especially that of the heart.
dysrhythmias: plural of dysrhythmia, which can refer to types of dysrhythmia, cases of dysrhythmia, or episodes of dysrhythmia.
dystaxia: a milder or weaker form of ataxia
dystocia: A slow or difficult labour or delivery.
dystonia: A disabling neurological disorder in which prolonged and repetitive contractions of muscles cause jerking, twisting movements and abnormal postures of the body.

dystopia: A miserable, dysfunctional state or society that has a very poor standard of living or severe censorship, oppression, etc.
dystopian: Of or pertaining to a dystopia.
dystrophy: A wasting of body tissues, of either genetic origin or due to inadequate or defective nutrition.
